Its MCP-compatible agent must analyze newly supplied maintenance notes using named entity recognition, key phrase extraction, and summarization. The notes are not questions to a curated FAQ. A Foundry resource/project, Azure Language resource, resource-group Contributor access, and authenticated project connection are already in place. Which integration is designed to expose these analysis capabilities as callable tools?

authoredQuestion.question: A maintenance application already uses Azure Content Understanding API 2025-11-01 with working supported model deployments to process text documents. Its downstream importer requires named fields for equipment, observed fault, and recommended follow-up. The team wants those fields defined in the analyzer's structured-output contract, rather than inferred later from narrative text. Which change fits that requirement?

answerChoices.text: Define the required field extraction schema in the analyzer and consume its structured JSON output.
Select Markdown output and let the importer infer the required fields from headings.
Keep the analyzer schema unchanged and treat a free-text request for JSON as the enforced field contract.

authoredQuestion.explanation: Configure the analyzer's field extraction schema and use the structured JSON result expected by the importer.
authoredQuestion.deepExplanation: Content Understanding separates the normalized content representation from schema-defined field output. A schema makes the requested output structure explicit; it does not make generated field values infallible. The scenario uses GA core document processing, not preview agentic document reasoning.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: Markdown supports reasoning and retrieval workflows, but asking the importer to infer fields does not define the requested analyzer field contract.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: A JSON instruction can guide a language model, but it is not the analyzer's field schema and does not by itself enforce compliance.

authoredQuestion.question: A preview Azure Language MCP integration is already authenticated and operational for supported English input. A feedback workflow has two separate jobs: assess the attitude expressed in each comment and obtain text with detected personal information masked before human review. Which pair of exposed capabilities matches those jobs?

answerChoices.text: Language Detection for attitude; PII redaction for the masked text
Named Entity Recognition for attitude; Summarization for the masked text
Sentiment Analysis for attitude; PII redaction for the masked text

authoredQuestion.explanation: Use sentiment analysis for expressed attitude and PII redaction for masking detected sensitive information.
authoredQuestion.deepExplanation: These are complementary tasks with different outputs. A language confidence score does not measure sentiment, and sentiment analysis does not redact personal information. The MCP integration is Preview; no aspect-level opinion-mining behavior, subtle emotion taxonomy, or perfect privacy guarantee is asserted.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: Language detection identifies a language and its confidence; it does not answer the attitude question.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: Entity recognition is not the requested attitude analysis, and a summary is not the service's PII-redacted version of the text.

Language tools/Core capabilities (line 38) exposes Sentiment Analysis and PII redaction independently. The PII lesson (lines 17-19, 50-58) explains identifying and masking sensitive personal information. The pair separates the two requested analyses without treating sentiment as a privacy control.

authoredQuestion.question: In an Azure AI Search index, Category is a filterable string field with no normalizer. A document stores the value shown below. A retrieval pipeline must include that document by exact Category equality, without full-text matching. Which filter matches?

answerChoices.text: Compare the first word: Category eq 'Safety'
Compare a lowercase literal: Category eq 'safety manual'
Compare reversed words: Category eq 'Manual Safety'
Compare the original literal: Category eq 'Safety Manual'

authoredQuestion.explanation: Category eq 'Safety Manual' matches the entire stored value with the same case. Exact filters do not perform full-text tokenization.
authoredQuestion.deepExplanation: A token search and an equality filter have different contracts even when both accept text. The explicit absence of a normalizer matters: the default comparison is case-sensitive. The reversed and shortened phrases also fail independently of case because they are different complete values.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: Equality filtering compares the whole string; it does not tokenize Safety Manual into words and match only Safety.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: With no normalizer, the comparison is case-sensitive. This value changes the case of both initial letters.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: Reordering the words changes the literal value. The filter does not analyze the words as an unordered set.
